headline: Uber expands beyond rides and delivery with hotels, boat rentals, and AV Labs
summary: Uber's CPO discusses the company's expansion into hotels, boat rentals, and financial services, emphasizing a focus on travel and strategic partnerships rather than becoming an "everything app."
details: Uber has quietly expanded beyond its core ride-hailing and delivery businesses. The app now features hotel bookings powered by Expedia, "shop for me" concierge services, and boat rentals in Europe.
Under the hood, Uber is also developing new initiatives. These include debit cards for drivers (the Uber Pro card) and a data-labeling side hustle for earners looking to supplement their income.

A six-month-old business unit called AV Labs is developing a fleet of sensor-equipped vehicles. This initiative aims to gather driving data, strengthening relationships with autonomous vehicle partners while also serving as a strategic hedge.

Chief Product Officer Sachin Kansal explained that travel is a key focus, with 1.5 billion trips annually occurring outside users' home cities. The introduction of hotels on Uber, in partnership with Expedia, is a major part of this strategy, complementing existing food delivery services.

Uber's financial services ambitions primarily target drivers and couriers through products like the Uber Pro card, allowing them to transfer earnings. The company is also experimenting with merchant-focused financial products in certain regions.
Kansal clarified that Uber is not striving to become a full-blown "everything app" like some Asian super-apps. Instead, its product strategy involves leveraging expert partners for specific services.

For new ventures like boat rentals, Uber may initially rely on a hand-off model to partners, allowing for quicker implementation. However, for strategic areas like hotels, deep integration with partners like Expedia allows Uber to build the entire user interface within its own app.

headline_marked: [[Turn your singing voice into printable notes]] directly in your browser
headline: Turn your singing voice into printable notes directly in your browser
summary: This innovative browser-based tool instantly converts your vocal performance into musical notation, complete with pitch, rhythm, and re-attack detection.
details: Sing into your microphone, and this browser-based tool instantly transcribes your vocal pitch into musical notation. A metronome sets the grid, ensuring accurate rhythm as it captures the pitch you hold in each subdivision.

Your fundamental vocal pitch is drawn against standard staff positions, with vertical lines indicating beats and darker ones marking downbeats. Pitches committed to the score appear as dots, while a red stem signifies a re-attack, creating a new note instead of a tied one.

The 're-attack sensitivity' feature is crucial for distinguishing between held and repeated notes of the same pitch. It detects subtle dips in volume between notes; if the quietest moment falls below a set fraction of the note's loudness, it's split into two separate notes.

For optimal results, using headphones is recommended to prevent microphone bleed from the metronome click. The tool also includes a noise gate to ignore quiet sounds and a pitch tolerance setting to filter out slides and scoops, ensuring only true semitones are recorded.
